themes_detail.label: NYPD Enforcement Surge
themes_detail.summary: Real Time Enforcement complaints spiked to 16 this week versus a baseline of 0.9 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 1,729% increase (z-score: 14.36)—suggesting a sudden, district-wide policing or ticketing operation began in the last 7 days.
evidence: 16 Real Time Enforcement complaints this week vs. 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1,729% spike, z-score 14.36)
Concurrent spike in IAD (Investigations and Discipline) complaints: 6 last week vs. 0.2 average (2,300% increase, z-score 13.28)
Both spikes emerged in the same reporting period with exceptionally high statistical significance
reporting_angles: What enforcement operation or policy change triggered the sudden surge in NYPD ticketing or enforcement actions in Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights this week?
Are residents experiencing targeted enforcement in specific neighborhoods or for specific violations, and what is the stated rationale?

themes_detail.label: Residential Disposal Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Residential Disposal Complaints jumped to 11 last week from a baseline of 2.5 per week—a 340% spike (z-score: 9.81)—indicating a sudden sanitation or waste management crisis affecting households across the district this week.
evidence: 11 Residential Disposal complaints last week vs. 2.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (340% spike, z-score 9.81)
Concurrent spike in Dead Animal complaints: 5 last week vs. 1.2 average (300% increase, z-score 4.52)
Both spikes suggest possible service disruption, pest infestation, or waste collection failure
reporting_angles: Has garbage collection been interrupted or delayed across Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights, and what is Sanitation's status on resuming full service?
Are residents reporting foul odors, pest infestations, or overflowing bins due to missed pickups?

themes_detail.label: Electrical Infrastructure Failures
themes_detail.summary: Electrical complaints surged to 6 last week from a baseline of 0.9 per week—a 586% increase (z-score: 5.53)—suggesting widespread power outages, wiring hazards, or grid strain in the district this week.
evidence: 6 Electrical complaints last week vs. 0.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (586% spike, z-score 5.53)
Spike is recent and localized to single reporting period, indicating acute event rather than chronic issue
No corroborating Reddit or news coverage yet, suggesting emerging story
reporting_angles: Have residents experienced power outages or electrical failures across specific blocks or buildings in Fort Greene or Brooklyn Heights this week?
Is Con Edison aware of any grid issues, outages, or infrastructure damage in the district requiring emergency repairs?

themes_detail.label: Park Safety & Animal Incidents
themes_detail.summary: Animal-in-Park complaints jumped to 10 three weeks ago from a baseline of 2.6 per week—a 281% spike (z-score: 4.1)—and Park Rules violations spiked to 3 from 0.2 average—a 1,100% increase—indicating emerging safety or wildlife conflicts in district parks.
evidence: 10 Animal-in-Park complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 2.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (281% spike, z-score 4.1)
3 Violation of Park Rules complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average (1,100% spike, z-score 6.35)
Both spikes point to simultaneous park safety or wildlife incident 3 weeks ago
reporting_angles: What animal incidents or safety problems prompted the spike in complaints at Fort Greene Park, Brooklyn Bridge Park, or other district parks three weeks ago?
Are Parks Department enforcement actions or wildlife management efforts underway to address recurring animal issues?

themes_detail.label: Building Code Violations
themes_detail.summary: Building/Use complaints spiked to 7 three weeks ago from a baseline of 1.4 per week—a 409% increase (z-score: 5.06)—suggesting possible illegal conversions, occupancy violations, or construction safety issues emerging in the district.
evidence: 7 Building/Use complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 1.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (409% spike, z-score 5.06)
1,208 DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (870 alterations), consistent with active construction activity
Active ULURP applications (395 Flatbush Ave Ext., Columbia Heights Rezoning) may be driving underlying development pressure
reporting_angles: Are Department of Buildings violations clustered around specific development projects or neighborhoods experiencing rapid construction?
What building code or occupancy violations are residents reporting most frequently as development activity accelerates?
